sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry confirmed cell-surface display; protease activity assays confirmed the HA tag does not affect testisin enzymatic activity. Both surface expression and function are preserved.
sites.rationale: PRSS21/testisin has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–19 (landmark-authoritative) and is entirely extracellular from residue 20 onward; there is exactly one extracellular N-terminus. The paper states the HA tag is at 'the N-terminus of testisin' with no residue number, so the junction is topology-derived: insert_after_residue=19, placing the tag between R19 (last signal-peptide residue) and K20 (first mature residue). Python confirmed seq[18]='R' and seq[19]='K'. L2 and L3 corroborate the same construct but provide no additional positional information beyond what L1 already establishes. Full-length membrane-anchored testisin expressed from pDisplay.Testisin carries an HA tag described as positioned at 'the N-terminus of testisin'; the construct was stably expressed in ES-2-Luc ovarian cancer cells and in lentiviral systems. The paper names no specific residue number.

sources.claim: The HA-tag is positioned at the N-terminus of testisin for ease of detection and has been shown not to affect testisin activity or cell surface expression [ 15 ].

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same HA-tagged testisin construct from the same laboratory (pDisplay.Testisin). L1 is the primary evidence because it explicitly states both the tag position ('N-terminus of testisin') and the functional validation (activity and surface expression unaffected). L2 and L3 confirm the construct was used in lentiviral and stable-cell-line contexts but add no new positional information; they are not promoted to separate sites. The S238A catalytic mutant mentioned in L2 identifies S238 as the active-site serine; this residue is recorded in other_positions. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: S238 is the catalytic serine of testisin; the S238A substitution produces a catalytically inactive enzyme, indicating this residue is essential for protease function and is not a permissive site for tag insertion.
